exact_unchanged_lines: ## 1. Core thesis

[GPE001] The Gourmet Research Society is held together by an appetite for experiences that its members do not experience in the same way. Haruna wants a relation among food, place, process and company; Akari wants abundance, lively company and recognition of her effort; Junko wants a meal she can actually enjoy within finite money and without interruption; Izumi wants unfamiliar tastes, but also wants other people to choose her company. Those differences produce a particular kind of ensemble: shared pleasure can be achieved without shared taste, while inclusion can be wanted without the earlier exclusion being repaired. The truffle sequence supplies the clearest miniature. Izumi's plea makes being left behind an injury to participation; the later group actually enjoys residual aroma rather than eating the truffle. A good common moment occurs, but it cannot make the earlier abandonment a willing sacrifice. (PUBLIC-02:L79–95; IZUMI-PRIVATE-09:L22–28; PUBLIC-05:L97–103.)

[GPE002] This is a literary argument about differentiated participation and unreliable mutual care. It does not assign the whole group one appetite, one conscience, or one permanent degree of affection. Akari can provide a clean wrapping and appeal to friendship while also teasing Junko past an objection; Haruna brings the kitchen oil and offers help. Junko can object and nevertheless contribute to the group's help. Izumi can delight in food others reject, acknowledge a recipient's ordinary preference and refuse to dine with a frightening version of her own club. Haruna can want a person's company enough to suspend destruction in one outing, yet refuse a restaurant owner's improvement chance elsewhere. The actual relation resides in these directed acts and responses, rather than in a presumed hidden harmony. (PUBLIC-02:L81–115; JUNKO-PRIVATE-06:L14–21; IZUMI-PRIVATE-11:L22–28; HARUNA-PRIVATE-05:L20–34; MAIN-09:L24–30; MAIN-20:L20.)

[GPE003] Quiet pleasure is part of the explanation, not a reward whose relevance has to be earned through rescue. A liked snack, an ordinary noodle meal, a notebook, an ornament whose explanation is withheld, shared mochi work, a cat, a returned greeting and the last messages after a MomoTalk launch witness disclose what each person wants from living with others. Public disorder tests those wants without exhausting them. Conversely, a completed meal, a cookie praised for its sincerity or a successful coordinated operation does not settle the rights of the provider, the costs borne by an absent member or the consequences for an owner. Pleasure and answerability need their own endpoints. (PUBLIC-01:L516–528; HARUNA-PRIVATE-02:L20–34; HARUNA-PRIVATE-11:L18–38; AKARI-PRIVATE-06:L14–40; PUBLIC-23:L168–176.)
## 2. Longitudinal arc and finite endings

[GPE004] The available longitudinal account is a comparison among source-local sequences, not a single dated growth ladder. GROUP1101 continues into 1102; 1103's account of yesterday's mint-related arrest does not establish its date relative to the truffle detention; 1104 starts a separate kitchen encounter. MAIN's soba destruction and later post-compulsion meal have their own chapter order. New Year and sports variants place particular clothes and circumstances around people; their labels and release contexts do not date every private meeting against MAIN. This matters because an undated refusal or destructive joke cannot automatically be labelled regression after an apology. The claims below instead retain what is achieved, reported, offered or withheld in each complete local ending. (PUBLIC-02:L45–60; PUBLIC-05:L78–87,133; PUBLIC-11:L23–40; MAIN-09:L18–30; MAIN-20:L18–26.)

[GPE005] GROUP1101 begins its decisive group problem with Izumi's recalled or dramatized plea, subsequently framed by Akari's report. It is not Izumi speaking beside the others in the park. Akari acknowledges leaving her behind; the proposed sacrifice language is checked by the plea itself. Junko's attention shifts the conversation toward aroma and the found truffle. Akari's pig comparison provokes Junko's objection, and the clean, previously unopened underwear becomes a practical wrapping. Haruna proposes rescuing Izumi before tasting. The order matters: wanting the absent member back is an actual intention, not an already accomplished rescue, and the police arrest interrupts rather than fulfils the planned meal. (PUBLIC-02:L68–87.)

[GPE006] GROUP1102 supplies local reunion and an actually shared sensory good. Chinatsu's promised return after an approximately month-long check remains a promise. Akari offers the residual aroma; Izumi first rejects the underwear association and then accepts its smell, Haruna praises it, and Junko continues to object to its impropriety. The scene therefore has differentiated uptake rather than one undivided approving audience. There is no completed truffle meal, verified release schedule or reciprocal account settling Izumi's earlier abandonment. Sensei's invitation and the later misunderstanding about the underwear add ordinary comedy and a hasty custody response, without printing death, durable safety or legal disposition. The sensory pleasure is neither imaginary nor sufficient repair. (PUBLIC-02:L91–97.)

[GPE007] GROUP1103 then makes disagreement over taste its own relation. Hare's fictional explanatory account and the reported informal tests are not biological proof of why Izumi and Haruna like something Junko and Akari reject. Izumi defends resemblance and affordability in the toothpaste-water sale account; Junko distinguishes enjoyment from suitability for sale. Izumi still enjoys it at the ending. The disagreement persists instead of being dissolved by a secret objective taste hierarchy. GROUP1104 ends more adversely: the offer of oil and help addresses Fuuka's reported impossible egg workload, but her warning is interrupted and no meal, cleanup, apology or repaired division of labor is narrated. An intention to help is positive evidence; success in providing care requires a further test. (PUBLIC-02:L101–115.)

[GPE008] EVENT820 extends that test through listening. A pleasant early New Year meal and Junko's praise of grilled fish are actual, while the bill has no printed payment. The proprietor's threatened closure prompts Haruna to recruit help coercively before knowing why the shop might close. Fuuka's later personal offer after hearing his account, and her new agreement after Haruna pauses and apologizes for forced contest work, are two source-local decisions. Neither reaches backward to authorize the capture. Customer tasting, differentiated budgets and the announced Suzume victory are stronger endpoints than mere plans, but future contracts, wages, layoffs, supply accounts and business survival remain unprinted. The festival coda preserves gratitude, food, wishes and comic renewed failure without announcing universal reform. (PUBLIC-05:L97–125.)

[GPE009] MAIN C001E009 supplies the severe countercase to an easy rescue arc. The first soba proprietor pleads for a chance; the proposed roughly one-week reprieve is refused, a blast occurs and he reports his shop gone. The physical trigger and precise damage are unprinted, but the threatened destruction and the refusal are clear enough to matter. The different nearby restaurant later joins the points partnership; it is not the destroyed shop restored under another label. MAIN C002E020 later gives Haruna's and Akari's actual apology for imposed food control, Izumi's fear and Fuuka's prospective refusal to cook if it recurs. A voluntary warm meal and changed address have been achieved. Restitution, a tested prevention mechanism and a complete account of every earlier owner or member have not. (MAIN-09:L20–30; MAIN-20:L18–20.)
## 3. Public and private selves

[GPE010] The private repertoire does not conceal a uniformly gentle real self behind a false public comic mask. It shows alternative ways of pursuing goods and responding to constraints. Haruna's elaborate preparation ends in an actual shared 100-yen noodle meal whose narrator calls the taste ordinary while she finds a difference; her reported repetition is less satisfying. Company, circumstances and technique remain serious competing explanations. Another outing explicitly denies that she destroys every disappointing shop and ends with a completed shared snack walk. New Year disappointment coexists with valued time, and mutual feeding with empty boxes has stronger support than a later invitation. Those actual acts qualify a destruction-only reading without cancelling the soba owner's experience. (HARUNA-PRIVATE-02:L20–34; HARUNA-PRIVATE-04:L20–36; HARUNA-PRIVATE-05:L20–34; HARUNA-PRIVATE-07:L20–32; MAIN-09:L24–30.)

[GPE011] Akari's public quantity and spectacle have private costs. Garlic pleasure leaves an embarrassing odor whose duration differs by locale; her wallet limits a shopping plan; mochi making takes work and receives gratitude, while promised tasting priority is not shown fulfilled. A narrated sixty-portions-in-thirty-minutes record and an announced winner can support local contest pride without proving sabotage, physiology or general superiority. She can withdraw a joke about a second shop when money becomes salient. These are conditions under which company is wanted and negotiated. Akari's practical wrapping in GROUP1101 and friendship appeal in GROUP1104 are thus more than evidence for manipulation, while Haruna brings oil and offers help; neither fact makes Akari's teasing welcome. (AKARI-PRIVATE-02:L14–36; AKARI-PRIVATE-03:L14–38; AKARI-PRIVATE-04:L14–38; AKARI-PRIVATE-05:L14–44; AKARI-PRIVATE-06:L14–40; PUBLIC-02:L83–115.)

[GPE012] Junko's private scenes preserve her own positive measure of food: actual modest noodle satisfaction, a notebook of criteria, privacy over its meaning, finite budget and the wish not to be described only through appetite. A future expensive meal is not completed, Sensei's offer to pay does not prove payment or notebook transfer, and a refused straw is not secretly accepted intimacy. New Year clothing, actual cakes and reciprocal greetings belong alongside anonymous strikes and meals she fails to receive. A character who objects so often can still want the club's familiar day and voluntarily help; she is neither a permanently detached commentator nor a person whose every protest is merely a joke awaiting reversal. (JUNKO-PRIVATE-02:L14–21; JUNKO-PRIVATE-03:L14–21; JUNKO-PRIVATE-05:L14–21; JUNKO-PRIVATE-06:L14–21; JUNKO-PRIVATE-07:L14–23; JUNKO-PRIVATE-09:L14–25; PUBLIC-11:L213,256.)

[GPE013] Izumi's curiosity includes generosity, caution and recipient attention. Extreme queue trades can be refused without the encounter ending; a cat-related bite and forgiveness do not establish immunity to future injury; an actual novel drink taste does not prove that Sensei drank before fainting or identify a toxic mechanism. Her commissioned New Year meal combines initiative, apology for leaving the adult out and reassurance, with no inspection of her own cooking. The final paired thread continues seventeen records after an interior BOND witness, through cold concern, thanks, the adult's ordinary or moderate preference and goodnight. Removing that quiet tail would make the curious eater less capable of attending to another person's preferred life than the full source permits. (IZUMI-PRIVATE-02:L22–28; IZUMI-PRIVATE-03:L22–28; IZUMI-PRIVATE-08:L22–28; IZUMI-PRIVATE-10:L22–28; IZUMI-PRIVATE-11:L22–28.)

[GPE014] Written profiles, normal dialogue and costumes add expression rather than a second performance of each bond. Junko's reading hobby and food-only resistance, Akari's anticipation and awareness that others may dislike chaos, Haruna's rest, tea, privacy and uncertain recognition, and Izumi's waiting, birthday remembrance, refused-hug accommodation and inquiry about a preferred food remain intrinsically meaningful. Reissued event lines retain different conditions and mechanical identities; equal words are not dozens of enacted encounters. A friendly written invitation does not establish a completed trip or global permission. These limits preserve the repertoire rather than disqualify it. (JUNKO-PRIVATE-10:L14–23; AKARI-PRIVATE-08:L14–40; AKARI-PRIVATE-10:L14–38; HARUNA-PRIVATE-12:L20–36; HARUNA-PRIVATE-15:L20–36; IZUMI-PRIVATE-13:L22–30; IZUMI-PRIVATE-14:L22–30; IZUMI-PRIVATE-16:L22–28.)
## 4. School and club role

[GPE015] The club's gastronomy vocabulary supplies affiliation and purpose, not automatic consent to whatever is done under it. Izumi's description of peers' different priorities is her own situated interpretation; the public sequences independently show differing wants rather than verifying every part of that report as doctrine. Haruna's claim that a second chance would be unfair to previously destroyed shops makes a retrospective principle out of coercion, while the proprietor remains an independently pleading recipient. Junko repeats a group motto while complaining about wood scattered into food. Belonging can therefore coexist with resistance inside the same exchange, and food seriousness can coexist with harm to another person's possibility of improvement. (IZUMI-PRIVATE-09:L22–28; MAIN-09:L24–30; PUBLIC-02:L79–87.)

[GPE016] The group can also articulate food as a relation to work, atmosphere and a place's history. EVENT820 gives that idea a generous object in the proprietor's inherited restaurant and care for customers. It also supplies correction: passersby have budgets and limited time, the anticipated regular-customer menu is only proposed, and Haruna admits overlooking price. Junko's interruption before one bite, Juri's pleasure in shopping and cooking, Fuuka's constrained labor and opposing workers' possible layoffs prevent the restaurant from becoming merely the gourmets' meaningful backdrop. To defend a place as a source of pleasure requires listening to people whose goods differ from one's own. The group sometimes learns to do this locally; no stable institutional mechanism is thereby installed. (PUBLIC-05:L101–123.)

[GPE017] EVENT841019 makes a constructive public capacity concrete. Owners' fear and stories of prior explosions survive the group's present offer of help. Taste is approved, Junko proposes discoverability through names and hashtags, Akari suggests a review incentive, the campaign is implemented and students arrive. Izumi can enjoy available food even when the imagined unusual takoyaki is absent, and Akari says she will restrain herself when Sensei worries about cost. This is actual useful participation and a local flourishing stall, rather than proof that every reputation was wrong. Haruna's retained broader punitive language keeps the countercase alive. The club can contribute without ceasing to be contestable. (PUBLIC-12:L1003–1019,1038.)

[GPE018] The institution represented by School Lunch is a distinct obligation. GROUP1601/1602 explicitly identifies Izumi as a visitor, not a member; her cookie and juice enjoyment cannot certify safe provision or authorize early consumption of communal meals. A favorable hygiene checklist, Iori's adverse response, safe waking and actual F rating are separate findings. Similarly, Fuuka's warm post-compulsion meal is voluntary work with a stated future boundary. This ensemble uses these recipient constraints to understand member participation; it does not claim completion of School Lunch's resource, evaluation or governance synthesis, nor the separate Gourmet→Fuuka directed relationship. No invented Gourmet institution is required to make the present group argument substantial. (PUBLIC-03:L53–106; MAIN-20:L20.)
## 5. Ordinary life and wanted pleasures

[GPE019] The truffle aroma is an especially useful ordinary endpoint because it offers less than the hoped-for meal and still offers something real. Junko's impropriety objection, Izumi's initial rejection and later sensory uptake, Akari's practical resource and Haruna's praise make the moment social rather than a uniform physiological reflex. The pleasure belongs at its scale: a shared smell in detention. It is not a substitute meal, a fulfilled rescue plan or proof that the group needed detention to become close. Its value is not reduced by the absence of any higher-stakes result. (PUBLIC-02:L91–97.)

[GPE020] Familiarity can itself be wanted. The EVENT818 afterstory gives Haruna enjoyment even with poor results and familiar rice and miso that do not tire her; Junko likes the day because it resembles ordinary club life; Akari enjoys a machine matching her pace; Izumi wants particular unusual flavors and roasting. These are different reasons to enjoy the same occasion. A relay ranking does not measure those goods, and the account does not show unanimous festival enjoyment: other recipients explicitly dislike the burdens. This lets the ensemble resist a novelty-only theory without treating familiar pleasure as a permanent taste law. The present receiving of this owner is the complete consequential argument at its stated lines, not a fresh whole receipt of its 201-record actor annex. (PUBLIC-11:L207–233,249–264.)

[GPE021] Small company is often achieved after a larger aim fails. Haruna can find preparation or auction process pleasing despite disappointing flavor, and her shared noodle meal need not be rescued by proof of an extraordinary recipe. Akari can enjoy working mochi and an outing despite a wallet limit. Junko's failed substitute food does not erase actual noodles or a wanted greeting. Izumi moves from disappointing food touring to actual enjoyable water play and help, while the proposed octopus meal is interrupted before a bite. To keep all four outcomes is to allow a wanted life wider than culinary conquest, while resisting a sentimental claim that good company makes every failure welcome. (HARUNA-PRIVATE-02:L20–34; HARUNA-PRIVATE-06:L20–34; AKARI-PRIVATE-03:L14–38; AKARI-PRIVATE-06:L14–40; JUNKO-PRIVATE-02:L14–21; JUNKO-PRIVATE-09:L14–25; IZUMI-PRIVATE-07:L22–28.)

[GPE022] Quiet self-presentation also regulates participation. Haruna wants recognition of a wing ornament, defers its explanation and asks to stop; the adult accepts that boundary before the actual arm-held venue tour. Junko's notebook has value without its private motive being surrendered. Izumi can accept that Sensei wants only the sentiment of a hug and wait until work finishes, even while loneliness is expressed. Akari's embarrassment over smell or appearance is not simply a device that tests consumption capacity. These private limits are not proof of peer consent in another scene. They supply an important interpretive discipline: attention to someone means leaving room for what they do not want to share or do. (HARUNA-PRIVATE-11:L18–38; JUNKO-PRIVATE-06:L14–21; IZUMI-PRIVATE-14:L22–30; AKARI-PRIVATE-02:L14–36.)

[GPE023] Gifts have unequal dyads and unequal endpoints. Akari's novice chocolate-contest nervousness and appreciation of company coexist with repeated pressure on other contestants and an unfinished adult share. Junko offers to pay for a simple two-person dango gift, but the interruption and arrest leave no actual taste or payment. Haruna's sudden feeding gives local pleasure without advance permission; a completed preparation and sweeter taste report do not isolate the chemistry of gratitude. EVENT810039 belongs to Fuuka: her shared meal and cocoa are an independent recipient comparison, not an Izumi gift or a fabricated fourth Gourmet gift. Keeping those differences prevents an ensemble of abundant treats from becoming a fictitious uniform record of reciprocity. (PUBLIC-13:L37–45; PUBLIC-14:L37–73; PUBLIC-16:L35–65; PUBLIC-15:L35–63.)
## 6. Crisis behavior and accountability

[GPE024] Public danger does not reveal the one true appetite that ordinary scenes hide. EVENT804006 gives Haruna a taste-and-atmosphere hypothesis, Junko a selling and carrying criticism, Izumi leftovers and jam, and Akari spectacle, with a Haruna/Iori actor seam attached to one line. It supplies no direct Sensei choice. EVENT835007/008 similarly distinguishes Haruna's active-discovery ideal, Akari's quantity, Izumi's actual enjoyment of the offered strange food and Junko's burn. Umika refuses the unlicensed product; the contextual Fuuka-function objection is not silently reassigned from the literal Haruna label. A locally achieved concession and a vanished stall do not establish capture or a finished licensing remedy. Their wants are legible and their methods remain answerable to a host. (PUBLIC-04:L81,95; PUBLIC-09:L103,141.)

[GPE025] FINAL-context defense is differentiated too. EVENT822007 preserves Haruna volunteering, Junko qualifying participation, Akari's enjoyment of destruction and Izumi's space-food wish. These speech acts do not prove that every defense task was performed or any food arrived. The accepted MAIN FinalC004E003 then gives maximum-speed pursuit and obstacle action before the destination is reached; E004 supplies Fuuka's arrival report and actual staged contribution by Haruna, Akari and Junko alongside Chihiro, Kayoko and Rio. Destroying the terminal and stabilizing a local operation are stronger conclusions than mere readiness. They neither establish universal rescue nor retroactively give freely chosen boarding or approval of earlier consumer demands. Competence is real at the finite operational endpoint. (PUBLIC-06:L96–104; PUBLIC-20:L22–34; PUBLIC-21:L20–32.)

[GPE026] The later escape account has another precise endpoint: Haruna proposes Fuuka first, and a written teleport association occurs without her own spoken report of arrival. Korean exhaustion wording is not supplied to Japanese, and neither locale establishes a complete destination or durable safety for every person. This prioritization is meaningful care; it is not a retrospective answer to all episodes in which Fuuka has been restrained. Likewise, the success of a party's compressed suppression can be retained while the separate group disturbance and missing repair details remain at group rather than falsely exact actor scope. A source can achieve a local operational good and still leave an ethical tail. (PUBLIC-07:L88–100; PUBLIC-08:L126–138.)

[GPE027] The MAIN post-compulsion meal gives the clearest explicit correction in the group's own words. Haruna admits forcing menus, supply timetables and surveillance; Akari rejects the controlling frame she imposed. Fuuka compassionately identifies them as victims too, but that is her response rather than an adjudication. Izumi says the changed club frightened her and will not dine with it if the conduct recurs. Fuuka's corresponding cooking boundary answers the same future. The scene joins a good meal, apology, fear and conditional participation instead of making forgiveness an automatic return to unlimited service. Akari's proposed strengthening against future brainwashing remains untested; narration that apologies convey feeling does not inspect repaired trust, property or institutions. (MAIN-20:L18–20.)

[GPE028] The complete MINI060 pair refuses an easier finale. The gourmets find Fuuka happily choosing ingredients; she forgot to contact Juri, so the initial inference of kidnapping is wrong. Mine's rescue intervention actually hurts or restrains people; Akari reports shielding Haruna and Haruna surrenders asking for appropriate treatment. The later cookies are actually completed, eaten and praised, and Haruna's praise of knowing the person rather than relying on rumor is a genuine generous countercase. Yet Fuuka is then actually bound and protesting while the others taste; Izumi's interpretation that she wants to hurry and cook is not consent. A reassurance to Juri conceals the restraint, Mine pursues and a tremendous chase ends the packet without release, returned lunch or repaired wall. The cookies remain good and the care remains unfulfilled. (PUBLIC-23:L166–176.)
## 7. Sensei relationship and independent recipients

[GPE029] Sensei is a participant with a finite appetite, work schedule and represented alternatives, rather than the device that guarantees shared pleasure. Akari's training company can end with the adult giving up; Izumi's invitations encounter ordinary or moderate preference, and Haruna's candy is strongly declined even while a joint return occurs. Junko's straw refusal does not need to become a hidden invitation for the adult's usefulness to remain visible elsewhere. Available choices and singleton records have their own branch identities; they are not every option simultaneously selected. These limits let student care, intrusion and recognition coexist with an independently bounded recipient. (AKARI-PRIVATE-01:L14–38; IZUMI-PRIVATE-11:L22–28; HARUNA-PRIVATE-10:L28–36; JUNKO-PRIVATE-05:L14–21; PUBLIC-02:L54–60.)

[GPE030] In the soba confrontation Sensei acknowledges bad taste yet seeks restraint, and the owner pleads independently. The unsuccessful roughly one-week proposal belongs to the committee's intervention, not a wish secretly granted by an omnipotent teacher. A later second-chance exchange opens an ethical possibility without restoring the destroyed venue. EVENT820 allows a captured teacher to doubt the coercive method, encourage listening and take inward responsibility at the ending; it does not make the adult the sole cause of Fuuka's chosen help or the proprietor's gratitude. The actual customers, merchants and workers also test the plan by their budgets, employment dependence, refusals and tastes. The group becomes more intelligible when those answers are retained outside teacher-centered interpretation. (MAIN-09:L24–30; PUBLIC-05:L99–131.)

[GPE031] Juri's EVENT844 ending supplies a particularly useful neighboring alternative, without giving its accomplishment to the gourmets. She offers pancakes while explicitly permitting refusal if recipients are afraid; Fuuka and Sensei accept, and narration confirms shared eating and sincere affection. Haruna's earlier ending presence recognizes varied household tastes, not the cause of the initial accident or ownership of Juri's learning. The positive food endpoint is neither discarded because workload continues nor transferred into a claim that Gourmet hospitality is now invariably respectful. A recipient's choice can change what a shared meal means. That distinction is a comparative result here, while School Lunch and the separate Gourmet→Fuuka argument retain their own required questions. (PUBLIC-10:L93–105.)
## 8. Major peer relationships and ensemble participation

[GPE032] **Members→Izumi: inclusion after abandonment.** The recalled plea and Akari's acknowledgement preserve an unwanted loss of participation. Haruna's rescue-before-tasting proposal recognizes a competing priority, but police custody prevents the plan from becoming an inspected rescue. Later presence and aroma-sharing are positive inclusion at their own scale; Izumi can reject the offered association before accepting its pleasure. Her present uptake cannot be substituted for a prior willingness to be left behind, and no apology or negotiated future inclusion rule is shown in this pair. The direction is therefore neither pure betrayal nor completed mutual repair: it is a member-facing failure followed by some actual re-inclusion and a still unanswered grievance. (PUBLIC-02:L68–97.)

[GPE033] **Izumi→members: taste, objection and continued choice.** Izumi's unconventional pleasure does not answer Junko's disgust or make her a willing sacrifice for everyone else's experience. Her New Year report distinguishes Haruna's experience, Akari's quantity-and-taste and Junko's uninterrupted or urgent eating, while keeping her own novelty seeking. She can enjoy the juice that distressed Iori and still support cleanliness; she can accept a prepared familiar meal without her usual sauce because the maker's care matters. Most decisively, her fear of the controlling club and future refusal to dine address belonging from her own side. The ensemble's continued existence does not establish that she would accept every demand made in its name. (IZUMI-PRIVATE-09:L22–28; PUBLIC-03:L96–106; MAIN-20:L20.)

[GPE034] **Akari→Junko: teasing beside useful provision.** Junko discovers the truffle aroma, and Akari's pig comparison turns that perception into a teasing hierarchy. Junko objects. Akari subsequently supplies the clean wrapping; in the kitchen Haruna brings oil and offers help, Akari invokes friendship, and Junko joins the help. Practical provision and the friendship appeal do not retrospectively make the insult welcome. Nor does Junko's participation demonstrate that every teasing remark is harmless. Her specific response remains evidence of a boundary even when she stays with the group. This directed relation depends on the opposition and continued practical association together, not on naming one member the playful speaker and another the humorless receiver. (PUBLIC-02:L83–87,111–115.)

[GPE035] **Junko→Akari and the group: resistance without withdrawal.** Junko repeatedly questions the group's rationalizations: the sacrifice language, suitability of a mint-like product for sale, menu respect, and MINI060's euphemism of asking Fuuka. Those objections may coexist with minimization of a terrorist label, participation in help or pursuit of food. She is not an external prosecutor with no share in the group's appetite. EVENT820 gives her real grilled-fish satisfaction and then an interrupted meal; EVENT841 gives practical promotional advice; EVENT818 gives pleasure in an ordinary club-like day. These positives do not cancel her objections, and her objections do not cancel her wanted membership. (PUBLIC-02:L79–115; PUBLIC-05:L97–109; PUBLIC-12:L1011–1019; PUBLIC-11:L213,256; PUBLIC-23:L168.)

[GPE036] **Haruna↔members: ideals answered by differentiated appetite.** Haruna's standard can coordinate attention to atmosphere and a threatened place, but it does not make Akari's volume, Junko's budget or Izumi's experiments lesser versions of the same aspiration. EVENT820's customer budgets correct a neglected consideration, and the member reactions inside the contest and festival likewise test her frame. At the same time, Haruna's desire to include Izumi and her defense of shared sensory experience are actual positive relation-making. Her admission that she might have exploded the cookie classroom if disappointed preserves pressure beside generous praise. This reciprocal ensemble question remains distinct from any independent directed home concerning a particular provider or member; substantial contextual directions here give the group mechanism its required specificity without completing another package by proxy. (PUBLIC-02:L85–95; PUBLIC-05:L97–129; PUBLIC-23:L172–176.)

[GPE037] Help and pleasure are distributed beyond the four members. Fuuka, Juri, Hare, Chinatsu, Iori, the soba proprietor, the Suzume proprietor, merchants, tourists, stall owners and workers have different kinds of standing. A remembered plea, an interrupted warning, a stated taste, a price constraint, an adverse grade and an actual refusal are not interchangeable measures of disapproval.
